newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher on Wednesday compared to New York's previous close on marginal overseas buying and continued shortcovering in very quiet trade, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$346.10/346.60 an ounce against New York's US$345.60/346.10 close on Tuesday.
"There was only a little European buying in the afternoon," said one bullion trader.
Others said the market remained slightly short and that Wednesday's buying activity likely was shortcovering.
"This has been the quietest day all month," said a gold trader at an international bank.
Market sentiment was leaning towards bullishness and dealers said they were optimistic gold would test $347 per ounce.
Demand in Asia for physical gold was slowing slightly as the price edged upwards, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$3 lower at HK$3,204 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -4.90 compared to its previous fix at +8.00.
